# fabric_item_job (Resource)

The Item Job resource allows you to manage a Fabric [Item Job](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/fundamentals/job-scheduler).

-> This resource supports Service Principal authentication.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "fabric_item_job" "example" {
  workspace_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  item_id      = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"
  job_type     = "Execute"
}

# Trigger a Data Pipeline on-demand with parameters
resource "fabric_item_job" "with_parameters_example" {
  workspace_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  item_id      = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"
  job_type     = "Execute"
  execution_data = jsonencode({
    parameters = {
      param_name = "param_value"
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `item_id` (String) <i style="color:red;font-weight: bold">(ForceNew)</i> The item ID.
- `job_type` (String) <i style="color:red;font-weight: bold">(ForceNew)</i> The job type. For a Data Pipeline use `Execute`.
- `workspace_id` (String) <i style="color:red;font-weight: bold">(ForceNew)</i> The Workspace ID.

### Optional

- `execution_data` (String) <i style="color:red;font-weight: bold">(ForceNew)</i> The execution data for the on-demand job, as a JSON encoded string. For a Data Pipeline this is where per-run pipeline parameters are passed, e.g. `jsonencode({ parameters = { param_name = "param_value" } })`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `end_time_utc` (String) The job end time in UTC.
- `failure_reason` (Attributes) The error response when the job has failed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--failure_reason))
- `id` (String) The Item Job instance ID.
- `invoke_type` (String) The job invoke type.
- `root_activity_id` (String) The root activity ID to trace requests across services.
- `start_time_utc` (String) The job start time in UTC.
- `status` (String) The job status.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--failure_reason"></a>

### Nested Schema for `failure_reason`

Read-Only:

- `error_code` (String) A specific identifier that provides information about an error condition.
- `message` (String) A human readable representation of the error.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# terraform import fabric_item_job.example "<WorkspaceID>/<ItemID>/<JobType>/<JobInstanceID>"
terraform import fabric_item_job.example "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111/Execute/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"
```
